title: FTSE Russell US indexes — annual June reconstitution, implemented after the close
source: EST: rule-derived from the index owner's own ground rules, no 2027-dated calendar reachable. FTSE Russell, "Russell US Equity Indexes" construction and methodology, v7.2, August 2026, fetched direct 2026-09-06 from lseg.com/content/dam/ftse-russell/en_us/documents/ground-rules/russell-us-indexes-construction-and-methodology.pdf (HTTP 200, 746,491 bytes, 50 pages) and text-extracted by this session. Appendix F, "Reconstitution schedule and applicable updates", states the June semi-annual reconstitution's Implementation as the "4th Friday of June", and defines it: "Implementation is the day changes are made after the close of the market and become effective at the open on the Monday following." June 2027's Fridays are 06-04 / 06-11 / 06-18 / 06-25, so the fourth is 2027-06-25 and the changes are effective at the open Monday 2027-06-28; 2027-06-25 is a full NYSE session (the only June 2027 closure is Friday 06-18, per nyse.com/markets/hours-calendars, HTTP 200, 109,180 bytes, fetched direct the same session). The same appendix dates Rank Day to the "Last business day of April" (2027-04-30) and the preliminary announcement to five weeks before implementation. Filed estimate, not confirmed, because this is the standing rule applied forward: no FTSE Russell 2027 reconstitution calendar was reachable to this runner -- lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/index-reconstitution and the dam-hosted 2027 recon-calendar PDF both returned 404, and lseg.com/en/ftse-russell/russell-reconstitution returned HTTP 200 but renders client-side and extracted to 838 characters of no content. Promote on a published FTSE Russell 2027 recon calendar naming 2027-06-25. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: PROPOSED by the sp-select-sector-secondary-reweight-2027-06-30 initial research (2026-09-06) because it lands INSIDE that event's drift window and two sessions before its 2027-06-29 trigger test -- the +/-5-day corridor around 2027-06-30 held exactly two tracked entries before this proposal (consumer-confidence-2027-06-29, fomc-minutes-2027-06-30), and what it was missing is the largest scheduled single-day forced-trade event in the US equity calendar. WHY IT MATTERS TO THE PROPOSER: the Select Sector secondary test measures capped index weights at the 06-29 close, seven sessions after the 06-17 rebalance re-caps everything; recon price impact on 06-25 and its subsequent reversal land squarely inside that measurement window. THE PROPOSER MEASURED THE EFFECT RATHER THAN ASSERTING IT, and the result is a negative: across the 10 actual June drift windows 2017-2026 (seven sessions ending on June's second-to-last business day, each containing that year's recon), AMZN cleared the +4.35% relative-to-XLY move that would re-open a single-name breach in 1 of 10 -- 10.0%, against a 10.3% unconditional seven-session base rate on the same 10-year tape. So this entry is filed as a real, dated, large flow event that a corridor should know about, NOT as evidence that June's drift window is hotter. Impact medium rather than low: it is market-wide, mechanically forced, and reliably the year's heaviest US closing auction, but no house playbook is index-flow- or calendar-keyed (trade-playbooks.md and multi-symbol-sweep.md grepped 2026-09-06 for rebalanc|index effect|select sector|capping|secondary reweight|reconstitution, zero hits), so it widens caution and licenses nothing. Kind `sector` matches the sibling market-structure flow entries; the enum has no index-flow member and the imperfect fit is named, not fixed from this lane. Estimate status is the honest one until a published 2027 calendar is reachable.
